solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Diamond, for example, that's useful when dating

definitions.meaning: diamond is a crystalline form of the element
radiocarbon dating measures the age of ancient remains

explanation.surface: Advice that a diamond ring helps when courting someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The romance is a decoy: the dating here is the scientific kind, where archaeologists measure carbon-14 to age old organic material.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamond is one crystalline form of the chemical element, an example of it in pure state.

clue.text: Article difficult to believe in any way

parts.note: as in an exaggerated story that is hard to credit

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece that no reader could swallow in any respect.
explanation.walkthrough: A tall tale is an exaggerated, unbelievable one.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are emphatic fillers meaning whatsoever, used in questions or negatives such as 'not in any way'.

clue.text: Gamble about two guys providing cover for patient, perhaps

indicators.note: the gamble goes round the outside of the two guys, as a fence is about a field

parts.note: two men's names, Ed and Jack

explanation.surface: Someone wagering on a pair of men who will shield a hospital patient.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords freely turn 'guy' or 'man' into any short male name; here ED and JACK sit side by side inside BET.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed jacket is a short warm top worn when sitting up in bed, typical of invalids.

clue.text: Scientist from century long past? Yes and no

parts.note: 'no' to long past means the opposite of old
a hundred, as in cricket or darts slang

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a scientist really belongs to a bygone age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no' splits the phrase: yes to the century, which stays as TON, but no to long past, which flips to its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton was the English physicist who formulated gravitation and laws of motion.

clue.text: Took control of a lot of characters in the first eleven

definitions.meaning: seized command by force, past tense

definitions.text: a lot of characters in the first eleven
definitions.note: describes the spelling of the word rather than its meaning
definitions.meaning: eight letters, every one drawn from the first eleven of the alphabet, A to K

explanation.surface: A takeover of a sports team full of colourful personalities.
explanation.walkthrough: The first eleven is the top team, but here it means the alphabet's opening eleven letters, A to K; every letter of the answer is drawn from them.
explanation.definitionFit: To hijack is to seize command of a vehicle or thing by force, a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Object that's attractive, luckily?

parts.note: surface: something charming that happens to bring good fortune
setter: attractive in the physical sense of pulling iron, shaped like the traditional good-luck charm

explanation.surface: A charming object that also brings good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Attractive means magnetic, not good-looking, and luckily points to the U-shaped charm hung over doors for luck.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a U-shaped magnet, bent like the lucky charm, that pulls iron towards its poles.

clue.text: One of many Popes with his edict for our representative

parts.note: more popes have taken this name than any other
a papal bull is a formal decree from a pope

explanation.surface: A pope issuing a decree on behalf of our nation.
explanation.walkthrough: John Bull is the stout cartoon Englishman who personifies England, as Uncle Sam does America; 'our' is the British setter speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure is the national personification of England or Britain, standing for the whole country.

clue.text: Article by young reporter from tropical island

parts.note: a cub reporter is a novice journalist

explanation.surface: A news story filed by a junior journalist sent from a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' lets the article sit beside the reporter, so the pieces read in the reverse of clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something belonging to Cuba, the largest Caribbean island.

clue.text: Be without special term for fanatic

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of outside, so 'be' wraps round the other piece
a special arrangement of 'term' is not its usual order

parts.note: used as it stands, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A zealot is someone who does without a particular label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking, but here it has its older meaning of outside, as in the hymn line 'a green hill far away, without a city wall'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns describe a person holding radical views and pursuing them with excessive zeal.

clue.text: Value of magical device yielding part of our capital

parts.note: a wizard's stick, made possessive by 'of'

explanation.surface: The price of a magic gadget that conjures up a slice of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Value of magical device' is simply the wand's worth, read as one run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandsworth is a borough of south-west London, which is the British setter's capital city.

clue.text: Cask of wine is hit with head

definitions.meaning: a large barrel for wine or beer
as a goat strikes with its horns

explanation.surface: Someone struck by a barrel of wine, or headbutting it.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are unrelated words that happen to share a spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a large barrel holding about 126 gallons; the other is a verb for ramming someone forehead-first.

clue.text: In solitary, place limits on criminal

indicators.note: an instruction to put one piece inside 'solitary'

parts.note: a cap is a ceiling or limit

explanation.surface: Restricting a convict held in solitary confinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In solitary' reads as prison talk, but it is the container instruction, and 'place limits on' only fakes a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster of the Prohibition era, jailed for tax evasion.

clue.text: Bishop needs to get cross in old car

parts.note: cross as in annoyed, so the noun anger

explanation.surface: A churchman who is bound to lose his temper driving an ancient car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' is an adjective on the surface, but it gives the matching noun. A banger is British slang for a battered old car.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a banger is a noisy, dilapidated motor vehicle past its best.

clue.text: Pack for America in part of ship

definitions.meaning: the American word for a pack of playing cards
a floor level of a vessel

explanation.surface: Stowing luggage bound for the United States somewhere aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' looks like a verb about luggage but is the noun for a set of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: US usage calls a set of playing cards a deck; on vessels it is a horizontal floor level.

clue.text: Change in clue, too, in manner of speaking

indicators.note: an order to alter the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone altering a crossword clue so it reads more like natural speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' belongs to the letters, the second one is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Elocution is the skill or style of clear, expressive speech and pronunciation.

clue.text: In hospital, frantically solicit this kind of treatment

indicators.note: doing something frantically means doing it wildly, so the word following is thrown about

explanation.surface: A patient in a ward desperately begging for alternative medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: 'this kind of' needs a word describing treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Holistic medicine treats the whole person, mind and body together, rather than isolated symptoms.

clue.text: Volatile star raves, upon being disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed letters are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: A temperamental celebrity who rants when interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volatile star' paints a diva, but the star is an astronomical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is a massive stellar explosion, the most violent event in a star's life.

clue.text: European getting fired is extremely shocked

explanation.surface: A worker from the continent is stunned to lose their job.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a single sentence, but it splits cleanly into two halves plus the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Poleaxed originally meant felled by a battle axe, and figuratively means utterly stunned or dumbfounded.

clue.text: Pay with tenner, say, for extra information (low-down)

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote, one example of a note

explanation.surface: Handing over a ten-pound note to buy some inside gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low-down' looks like slang for inside information, but it literally means placed low, at the bottom of a page.
explanation.definitionFit: A footnote adds supplementary comment printed at the bottom of a page, beneath the main text.

clue.text: Gently touch husband, in a way

explanation.surface: Tenderly touching one's spouse in a certain manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' reads as a hedge meaning somewhat; split it, and 'a way' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a track or route along which one walks, so a road or route.

clue.text: Energy needed in forward line to get ahead

indicators.note: the energy is required inside the phrase 'forward line'

parts.note: a prop is a front-row forward in rugby

explanation.surface: A rugby coach wanting more energy from the front row to gain an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the prop is a forward in the front row of the scrum; E drops between PROP and L.
explanation.definitionFit: To propel is to drive or push something forward, moving it ahead.

clue.text: Discover doctor breaking law

indicators.note: the doctor breaks into 'law', splitting it open

parts.note: Bachelor of Medicine, a British medical degree

explanation.surface: Finding out that a physician has broken the law.
explanation.walkthrough: To rumble someone is British informal for seeing through their scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, to rumble is to find out the truth about a person or plot.

clue.text: Prolific scorer, having extra time a lot

indicators.note: the composer takes on an additional piece inside himself

parts.note: the composer wrote a vast number of scores

explanation.surface: A goal-hungry striker playing extra time scores plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prolific scorer' suggests football, but the scores are musical ones, written by J S Bach.
explanation.definitionFit: A batch is a quantity or group produced or handled together, a set.

clue.text: Flier to publicise handiwork

parts.note: to air a view is to make it public

explanation.surface: A leaflet printed to advertise homemade goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' looks like a handbill, but it is anything that flies.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane or helicopter is a machine that flies, so something that travels through the sky.

clue.text: Old prison ships

definitions.meaning: a London debtors' prison beside a river of the same name, closed in 1842

explanation.surface: Decommissioned vessels once used to hold convicts.
explanation.walkthrough: Prison ships, or hulks, really existed, which makes the phrase look like one idea rather than two.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fleet was a historic London jail named after its river; a navy's vessels together form a group.

clue.text: It shows up in performing, if talented

definitions.text: It shows up in performing, if talented

indicators.note: the letters make an appearance inside the neighbouring words

parts.note: straddles the end of the first word, the whole second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Real talent reveals itself on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also defines the answer: natural ability is what shines through when a talented person performs.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is a natural talent or aptitude, which becomes visible when someone gifted performs.

clue.text: Chauvinistic types wrecking phoneboxes

indicators.note: wrecking something smashes it, so its letters are broken up

explanation.surface: Bigoted thugs vandalising telephone kiosks.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters are used exactly, a pleasingly exact match.
explanation.definitionFit: Such people are prejudiced against foreigners, an aggressive national pride akin to chauvinism.

clue.text: At exactly the right time, then, to do otherwise

indicators.note: 'otherwise' asks for the letters in a different way from how they stand

explanation.surface: Deciding at the perfect moment to change one's plans.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'to do otherwise' reads as changing course; mechanically it just rearranges the small words.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means precisely punctual, as when a clock's hand reaches the exact mark.

clue.text: Slowly covering a structure on side of building

indicators.note: the tempo word covers the article, enclosing it

parts.note: the musical direction to play slowly

explanation.surface: Gradually cladding an extension attached to a house.
explanation.walkthrough: Italian tempo markings like lento are standard crossword fare.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a shed-like annex whose sloping roof rests against an existing wall.
